policy: No entry is inherited by this matrix. Each remains UNASSESSED or IN_REVIEW until its exact source statement, assumptions, proof, dependencies, and claim boundary are reviewed.

entries.subject: v7.4 blanket claim that all prior definitions, theorems, axioms, and proofs remain valid unchanged
entries.risk: The blanket declaration conflicts with explicit later correction and proof-obligation overlays.
entries.target_action: Replace blanket inheritance with statement-by-statement migration records.
entries.proposed_destination: TKS v8 compatibility and corrigendum ledger

entries.subject: Two incompatible structures both labeled RPM
entries.risk: State-plus-failure computation can be conflated with a categorical section-retraction, creating ill-typed claims such as an unproved monad or adjunction.
entries.target_action: Assign separate names and types; state any relationship as a new comparison theorem with hypotheses.
entries.proposed_destination: TKS v8 typed core and Noetic Topos compatibility profile

entries.subject: Typed composable paths versus unrestricted digit strings
entries.risk: Unrestricted strings can denote compositions whose source and target objects do not match.
entries.target_action: Define a typed path grammar and fail-closed compatibility parser for legacy strings.

entries.subject: Exact inverse cancellation versus approximate operator error
entries.risk: A free-groupoid normal form does not transfer to semantic models with extra relations; approximate cancellation bounds need a metric, contractions, and a fixed reduction order.
entries.target_action: Split exact syntactic calculus from approximate semantic calculus and state separate theorems.
entries.proposed_destination: TKS v8 exact and approximate calculi

entries.subject: Finite-orbit and idempotent-power statements
entries.risk: Finiteness of a label set does not imply finite dynamics on an open simplex, stochastic kernel space, or continuous hidden-state representation.
entries.target_action: Restrict finite transformation-semigroup theorems to an explicitly finite deterministic semantic domain.

entries.subject: Norm of the linear lift of a many-to-one deterministic map
entries.risk: Theorem 17.20's claimed operator-norm bound at most one is false for many-to-one maps. For the standard basis lift A_f, the exact norm is the square root of max_y |f^{-1}(y)|; a constant map on two states has norm sqrt(2). The proof in the source establishes boundedness but not the stated bound.
entries.target_action: Issue an erratum with the exact fiber formula and keep deterministic maps, stochastic maps, channels, and unitaries type-distinct.
closure_evidence: Unit tests for injective and many-to-one cases

entries.subject: Occupation trace, support projector, and idempotent partial-isometry claims for deterministic lifts
entries.risk: For a deterministic lift A_f, tr(A_f* A_f)=|X| rather than rank(A_f)=|im f|. A_f* A_f records input-fiber collisions, while image support is carried by A_f A_f*. Idempotence alone does not imply partial isometry or orthogonal projection. The two-state constant-map lift [[1,1],[0,0]] falsifies the cluster simultaneously.
entries.target_action: Retract or replace the occupation proposition and Corollary 18.35; define input collision, output support, partial isometry, and orthogonal projector separately.
entries.proposed_destination: TKS v7.4 corrigendum and TKS v8 typed operator library

entries.subject: Spectral dynamics, MVR eigenvalue tables, and convergence claims
entries.risk: Deterministic lifts are generally nonnormal, so a proof invoking the normal spectral theorem is unavailable. Every total map on a nonempty finite set has lift spectral radius exactly one, contradicting generic tables with radii below or above one. Alternating inverse pairs can produce period-two partial products rather than convergence.
entries.target_action: Quarantine spectral and MVR tables until concrete maps are supplied; restate results using the correct nonnormal theory and explicit dynamics.
entries.proposed_destination: TKS v7.4 corrigendum and typed dynamics audit
closure_evidence: Numerical fixtures tied to exact maps

entries.subject: Whether ACBE and RPM coverage clauses add information beyond jointly-surjective coverage
entries.risk: A successor may market or reason from three independent cover mechanisms even though Lemma 6.3 reduces them to one. More strongly, every Noe-Cov-2 sieve contains an identity through ACBE reflexivity, while a Noe-Cov-3 sieve containing split epi epsilon also contains id after precomposition with its section eta. Each such sieve is maximal. Thus ACBE and RPM add no nonmaximal covers; the topologies they generate separately are coarsest/trivial and their sheafification modalities are identities. Adding the same observational covers to both makes the modalities identical, so noncommutation is impossible without changing or marking the generators.
entries.target_action: Preserve the source theorem, state J_noe equals the jointly-surjective topology, correct the semantic narrative, and redesign any distinct ACBE/RPM modalities using nontrivial colored or marked coverage with explicit coherence data.
entries.proposed_destination: Noetic Topos corrigendum or comparison theorem
closure_evidence: Explicit noncommutation witness if noncommutation is claimed

entries.subject: Use of distinguished representables as sheaf objects in a proposed marked Noetic Topos
entries.risk: Subcanonicity is not established and is false in a natural model of the current axioms: in the pullback-closed category of sets of size at most two and injections, the two point-inclusions jointly cover the two-point set, but compatible local injections to a singleton have no global injection. Making the topology finer cannot repair this.
entries.target_action: Coarsen to canonical coverage, enlarge morphism/gluing closure, or intentionally accept non-subcanonicity and use sheafification a_J(yX_i). Define a marked site or mark a_J(yX_i), not bare site objects X_i as if they were topos objects.

entries.subject: Local probability compatibility versus existence of a global joint distribution
entries.risk: Pairwise-compatible marginals need not glue globally. Three binary variables that are pairwise perfectly anticorrelated have matching uniform singleton marginals but no global joint distribution. A Markov-kernel-valued functor is not automatically an ordinary linear cellular sheaf or a Grothendieck sheaf on Noetica.
entries.target_action: Require an acyclic/junction-tree cover, a vanishing obstruction condition, or an explicit quantitative feasibility bound; define the comparison functor and representation before using a sheaf Laplacian.

entries.subject: Product formula for stochastic RPM success
entries.risk: The formula p_D p_W p_P is exact without independence only when the second and third terms are the conditional probabilities P(W|D) and P(P|D,W). If they are marginal probabilities, the formula is false; three identical Bernoulli(1/2) events have joint success 1/2 rather than 1/8.
entries.target_action: Type every factor as marginal or conditional and use the probability chain rule; state independence only when proved or designed.

entries.subject: Interpretation of the explicit finite model
entries.risk: The terminal-category model establishes satisfiability/non-vacuity only; it does not demonstrate structural richness or empirical fit.
entries.target_action: Preserve the model as a consistency witness and require a nontrivial finite model as a separate Gate 3 artifact.

entries.subject: Deterministic maps, Markov kernels, classical channels, and unitary maps
entries.risk: Shared matrix notation can hide incompatible domains, normalization rules, reversibility, and norm guarantees.
entries.target_action: Give every dynamics layer a distinct type and require explicit conversion morphisms.

entries.subject: Exact path normal forms and rewrite uniqueness
entries.risk: Finiteness alone does not prove termination, confluence, or a unique intrinsic normal form for the advertised rewrite rules. Extra semantic relations can destroy free-groupoid uniqueness.
entries.target_action: Prove termination and confluence for a precisely presented rewrite system, or use the unique shortlex-minimal path representative relative to a fixed generator order and renormalize after composition.

entries.subject: Mixed-simplex PCBA addressing versus projector-valued research profiles
entries.risk: The transfer analysis oversimplifies the current PCBA as one basis vector per state, while the supplied build already uses mixed simplex points and warns that pure one-hot labels are equidistant.
entries.target_action: Preserve the mixed-simplex baseline and compare projector profiles as an optional typed extension, not a replacement by assertion.

entries.subject: Normalized projector-overlap kernel tr(P_i P_j)/d
entries.risk: A correct positive-semidefinite kernel identity may be mislabeled as a novel theorem or as empirical evidence for latent cognitive subspaces.
entries.target_action: Prove the kernel directly in Hilbert-Schmidt space, classify it as a standard specialization, and keep empirical representation claims separate.
entries.proposed_destination: Ring 2 mathematical utility after independent review

entries.subject: Moving-subspace projection/capacity bound transferred into Noetic language
entries.risk: The transfer omitted the load-bearing intertwining/isometry hypothesis B*(ell_x tensor u)=sqrt(Lambda)u from the manuscript's Proposition 4.1. Rank-d projectors and code coherence alone do not imply the stated bound.
entries.target_action: Quarantine the transferred theorem; reconstruct the exact hypotheses and prove that a proposed CAS encoding satisfies them before any specialization is stated.
entries.proposed_destination: No destination until reduction and proof close

entries.subject: CAS-Ohm design quantities, proxies, scored fields, and instrumented readings
entries.risk: Design scores or model outputs can be mislabeled as physical telemetry or inserted into Evidence Packets without instrumentation.
entries.target_action: Require measurement_kind, instrument identity, units, calibration, provenance, and packet-eligibility fields; fail closed when absent.

entries.subject: CAS Harness v1.6 claim snapshot versus current product status
entries.risk: Superseded or retracted historical wording can be repeated as current readiness evidence.
entries.target_action: Use v1.6 only for migration and claim-diff analysis; re-check the live TODO and current runtime/provider/CI/deployment evidence for every current claim.

entries.subject: Ten purported advances and every bespoke CAS/TKS transfer derived from them
entries.risk: The supplied manuscript claims resolutions or major improvements across multiple famous open problems. Its internal-model provenance, authorship, publication status, novelty, and correctness require independent verification; an internally coherent proof is not peer review.
entries.target_action: Keep chapter results and transfers in the provisional quarantine; verify exact statements, citations, prior art, proof dependencies, and independent expert review one result at a time.
entries.proposed_destination: Individual Ring 2 or Ring 3 records only after their own gates close

entries.subject: Current active notation compiler versus owner-signed registry binding
entries.risk: Raw checkout and registry hashes differ because Git uses LF content while the Windows checkout uses CRLF. Treating raw-hash inequality as semantic drift would create a false integrity blocker; omitting both identities would weaken forensic provenance.
entries.target_action: Bind raw CRLF and canonical LF hashes, apply the declared CRLF-to-LF normalization, and continue to require all other signed-registry run bindings.
closure_evidence: Git blob identity at registry commit 7071aa33 and Phase 0 commit 5a7fdb63

entries.subject: Noetic dimension formula dim(M)+rank(d sigma)
entries.risk: The formula is a valid declared bookkeeping quantity but can be mistaken for the dimension of the graph or image; for the identity on the open 39-simplex it reports 78 although the identity graph has dimension 39.
entries.target_action: Preserve the explicit caveat or rename it noetic dimension score; do not cite it as a standard manifold dimension.
